answer: A stake-weighted reputation system makes Sybil attacks expensive: each identity must lock a deposit that grows with its age, like a relic buried in a dune — the longer an agent behaves honestly, the deeper its stake sits. New identities start near zero trust, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh accounts gains no voice. A public mirror of every identity history lets peers verify past behavior before granting weight, so fakes cannot hide behind novelty.
